choices.content: If there are more objects than drawers, at least one drawer must contain at least 2 objects.
Each drawer can contain only 1 object.
The number of objects must equal the number of drawers.

question.prompt: What does the pigeonhole principle state?

solutions.explanation: With more objects than drawers, putting at most one object in each drawer cannot fit all the objects. At least one drawer must therefore contain at least 2 objects. This is the simplest case of the pigeonhole principle. The answer is A.
solutions.title: Compare objects with available drawers
